reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two claims as origin versus residence: Bethsaida was Peter and Andrew's native town, and Capernaum the home where they had since settled and where Jesus found them.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who lists Mark's Capernaum household against John's naming of Bethsaida as 'the city of Andrew and Peter' as a straightforward contradiction of place.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Where did Peter and Andrew live?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/peters_home.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; print ed. 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew; who being brethren, dwelt together in a house at Capernaum, where it seems they were now inhabitants, though their native place was Bethsaida, Joh 1:44 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Distinguishes native place (Bethsaida, citing John 1:44 by name) from where the brothers currently dwelt and were inhabitants (Capernaum) — the core reconcile move for this tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: the city of Andrew and Peter--of their birth probably, for they seem to have lived at Capernaum (Mar 1:29).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: States the resolving distinction in one line: Bethsaida as probable birthplace, Capernaum (citing Mark 1:29) as where they actually lived.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Bethsaida (“house of fishing”) was a village on Galilee’s north shore and the home of Peter, Andrew, and Philip. Later, Peter and Andrew moved to Capernaum, a village west of Bethsaida (Mark 1:21, 29).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Modern study-note version of the same harmonization: names Bethsaida as the disciples' original home and states plainly that Peter and Andrew later moved to Capernaum, directly citing Mark 1:21, 29.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), on "Peter's residence: Capernaum. Apparently Bethsaida" (Mark 1:21, 29 / John 1:44)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact passage pair by name, listing 'Peter's residence Capernaum. Apparently Bethsaida' and resolving it as native city (Bethsaida) versus later dwelling (Capernaum) — the same distinction the row's commentators draw.
